text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S. envoy Dennis Ross meets Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in effort to save peace process; Israeli army plans tough response to any violence ahead of Sunday's Land Day.
- Shoul Eisenberg dies in China, apparently of a heart attack at age 76. He was one of Israel's most influential industrialists.
- Howard Johnson, the American hotel chain, coming to Israel.
- Italian insurance company Assicurazioni Generali wants to meet Israeli members of parliament over Holocaust policies.
GLOBES
- Clal Israel profits drop 45 percent in 1996. Loss of a million shekels in fourth quarter.
- Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel: I'll back a managing council for the central bank -- of professionals obligated solely to the bank.
- Drop of 97 percent in Oil Refinery profits in 1996 to 3.8 million shekels.
- Qatar effectively renews indirect Arab Boycott on Israel.
HAARETZ

- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright demands from Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat a "red light" against terrorism. U.S. President Bill Clinton encouraged by Arafat's reaction to demand he fight terrorism. Warnings of attacks soon.
- Heads of Palestinian security apparatus reject Shin Bet secret service head Ami Ayalon's demand -- at meeting shortly after last Friday's Tel Aviv cafe attack -- that they act against terrorism.
- Israeli 98-room hotel planned beside Kalandia airport in West Bank which Israel calls Atarot airport.
- Interior Minister Eli Suissa calls for closing Tel Aviv streets to private vehicles.
MAARIV
- Message from U.S. President Bill Clinton: Calm now -- "assertive" peace initiative soon.
- Jailed American spy Jonathan Pollard says he doesn't like Netanyahu but doesn't know why, says Israeli leader is not real.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Police on record alert; "hot warning" of an attack.
- Poll shows 68 percent of Israelis worry terrorism will strike at them.
